sections.text:

The common legal name and ISIN remain consistent; later letterhead changes the activity portion of the CIN from U25203GJ2012PLC072513 to U19201GJ2012PLC072513, which is not treated as a rename or new security. The information cutoff is 20 October 2026 at 23:59 IST. Retrieval on 21 October does not admit post-cutoff information. The price date is 19 October because 20 October was an exchange holiday. Entry and terminal boundaries are 20 October 2026 and 20 October 2031. [S14][S17][S18][S28]

The historical base is standalone Indian GAAP accounting. The new UAE subsidiary was incorporated on 14 October and has no historical revenue. G1 is Conditional, not a severe integrity failure; G2 and G3 are Hold, and G4 is Hold for the illustrative ₹5 lakh new position. sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The 13 factor audits separate demonstrated business economics from unknown funding and implementation inputs. GOV 4, MOAT 3, REV 8, DUR 5, CAP 5, CASH 4, EXEC 5 and EARN 5 are evidence-based points; BAL, R, P and L remain NS. D is 4 for credible stress impairment, not an assertion that default occurred. REV uses the five-year manufactured-sales value CAGR, starting at 8 with zero trajectory adjustment and a Medium-confidence ceiling of 8. CAP uses a reconciled multi-year organic committed-capital substitute rather than one current ROCE number. EARN recognizes genuine operating growth but mixed sources; it is not mechanically reduced merely because inventory accounting contributes. [S01–S07]

Exact Decimal weighting gives BQS known contribution 4.26 with 92% coverage and missing-factor bounds 4.34–5.06; the final point is NS, not 4.6 or a renormalized value. GQS is exactly 6.10 with 100% coverage, displayed 6.1. IAS has only D scored, giving known contribution 0.80, 20% coverage and bounds 1.60–8.80; Q reuses the missing final BQS without imputation. No GOV≤3 or CAP/CASH≤3 numerical override is triggered. Nevertheless G2 prevents favorable investment classification and numerical quality rankings. Bounds are uncertainty intervals from missing weights, not probabilistic confidence intervals. Moving REV by ±1 changes GQS by ±0.40; CAP by ±1 changes it by ±0.15. These sensitivities cannot cure the gates.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The operating company converts waste rubber and tyre scrap into reclaim rubber and crumb used by tyre and other rubber-product makers. This is a physical manufacturing business with material, power, processing, yield and receivables costs, not a software-like recurring-revenue model. Manufacturing provided ₹20.632 crore of FY26 revenue, trading ₹16.8537 crore, EPR credits ₹2.2655 crore and other operating revenue ₹0.0696 crore. Trading was 42.32% of sales, versus 35.17% in the comparable FY25 standalone presentation. Gross turnover therefore overstates the rate of expansion in proprietary production. EPR is a legitimate operating revenue stream when recognized and realized, but its price and eligibility depend on the compliance market. [S01][S03][S06]

Management describes buying scrap around ₹20–25/kg and selling processed product around ₹45–50/kg. Those quoted ranges do not establish net unit profit: processing losses, grade mix, energy, freight, labour, maintenance, capital intensity, credit periods and returns must be deducted. Product-level cost allocation, verified annual physical tonnage and grade-level realizations are not sufficiently disclosed to compute a reliable actual manufacturing gross margin. The report therefore preserves gross profit as ND, while modeling tonnes, yields and external revenue separately as explicit assumptions. Pyrolysis input cannot simultaneously count as external crumb sales; internally used gas is not counted as a second external revenue stream. [S07][S08]

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text:
Access to waste tyres, consistent reclaim quality, proximity to consuming manufacturers and process know-how can create useful local operating advantages. The evidence does not yet demonstrate a durable cost leader, proprietary technology barrier or customer switching lock-in. The FY22 top-ten customer concentration was 94.20%; that is dated, and current concentration is ND, not assumed unchanged. Management says orders are repeated purchases rather than long-term contracts. Named large tyre-company relationships may include EPR services, so they cannot automatically establish product approvals or durable core manufacturing wallet share. [S06][S07]

Larger primary-source peers demonstrate both opportunity and economic friction. Tinna reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹545.8074 crore, PAT of about ₹52.85 crore and CFO of ₹57.4864 crore, far larger than Lead. GRP reported FY26 total income of ₹538 crore and EBITDA of ₹42.9 crore, with a ₹2.39 crore pyrolysis startup EBITDA loss; its EPR comparison also contains prior-period accrual. Hi-Green Carbon grew FY26 consolidated revenue to ₹138.6816 crore while PAT fell to ₹3.431 crore, illustrating that new recycling capacity does not guarantee proportional shareholder profit. These are contextual competitors, not interchangeable valuation multiples or completed peer ratings. Commodity feedstock/product spreads and startup costs remain central. MOAT 3 reflects limited demonstrated differentiation, not a claim that the company has no customers or useful processes. [S20–S22]

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text:
Reported sales rose from ₹7.035 crore in FY21 to ₹39.8208 crore in FY26, a 41.44% five-year CAGR, and from ₹8.76 crore in FY23 at a 65.65% three-year CAGR. The more conservative comparable manufacturing series rises from prospectus finished-goods sales of ₹6.9886 crore in FY21 to ₹20.632 crore in FY26, or 24.17% annually; FY23–26 manufactured CAGR is 36.91%. This is a value-growth proxy in a stable organic operating perimeter, not a claim that physical output compounded at the same rate. No meaningful acquisition revenue is added to the historical series. Ten-year comparable growth is ND because eleven verified annual observations are unavailable. [S01][S05][S06]

FY26 total revenue rose ₹8.697 crore, of which manufacturing contributed ₹2.6249 crore, trading ₹5.9064 crore, EPR ₹0.1554 crore and other operations ₹0.0103 crore. Thus most incremental gross sales came from trading; manufactured growth slowed to 14.58%. The standalone FY25 basis agrees with FY26 comparatives after rounding, but FY25 consolidated trading is ₹15.7774 crore rather than standalone ₹10.9473 crore despite the same headline turnover. This material mix discrepancy is preserved rather than silently used to change growth. The five-year selected basis earns REV 8, with no unsupported momentum bonus and no second small-base penalty. Price/volume and customer retention evidence would improve confidence. [S01][S03]

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The multi-year committed-capital calculation deliberately includes CWIP, capital advances and other advances instead of showing only commissioned fixed assets. Broad invested capital rose from ₹3.8844 crore in FY21 to ₹37.2907 crore in FY26. Normalized operating NOPAT at a 25% tax benchmark rose from ₹0.60825 crore to ₹4.815525 crore. The five-year incremental proxy is therefore 12.59%; the three-year proxy is 16.55%. A 13–17% nominal INR cost-of-capital range reflects small-company, commodity and financing risk rather than a spurious precise WACC. Returns are mixed around that range, supporting CAP 5. These ratios are not project IRRs: margin recovery on existing assets and EPR revenues contribute, and much new capital has not matured. [S01][S04–S06]

The investment annexure bridges fixed assets, working capital, advances and residual balance-sheet items, cross-checking cumulative cash capex less depreciation. Excluding EPR growth from incremental profit gives stress proxies of 7.51% and 9.95%, but does not assert that EPR is nonrecurring. Commissioned-only denominators can look better while wrongly excluding committed CWIP; no upgraded score is taken from them. The proposed EPDM and pyrolysis businesses require grade acceptance, yields, permits, capacity utilization and post-commission cash collections. Management capacity figures mix inputs, outputs and product lines, so the claimed 4,200 tonnes/month cannot be multiplied by a single realization. The runway is real enough for DUR 5, not strong enough for a compounder designation or unfinanced forecast certainty. [S07][S08]

sections.title: Management Governance and Execution
sections.text:
The FY26 main audit is unmodified and the separate internal-financial-controls opinion is positive. CARO reports no payment default or fraud, and September shareholding discloses no promoter pledge, non-disposal undertaking or other encumbrance. Those are meaningful counterweights. They do not resolve recurring failure to maintain accounting edit logs, contradictory bank-reconciliation disclosures, prior excess-remuneration approvals and the secretarial report’s MSME-1 filing lapse. GOV 4 reflects this opacity and compliance pattern without converting suspicion into a severe integrity allegation. The ₹1.10 crore advance to RBM Tyre Recycling, connected through an independent director’s spouse, equals roughly 4.55% of March equity and needs commercially evidenced delivery and settlement. Company arm’s-length assertions and repayment of smaller director/associate loans are retained. [S01–S04][S15]

July financing was material and verified, but ₹35.58 crore is the headline proposal, not cash already received. The known gross receipt is ₹14.60187 crore; future warrant exercise could add ₹19.18188 crore. EGM objects include working capital, debt reduction, expansion and general purposes/fees over two years, but not all proceeds were funded upfront. Capacity investment and revenue growth demonstrate some delivery. Conversely, the December 2026/March 2027 pyrolysis targets are future dates at the cutoff and are not falsely charged as missed. The September independent-director resignation cites other assignments and no other material reason; it is not presented as evidence of a dispute. EXEC 5 is mixed delivery, with future commissioning and output as the decisive next tests. [S07][S09–S11][S24][S25]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 operating EBITDA increased from ₹3.7058 crore to ₹8.5176 crore. The inventory-expense line swung by ₹4.3052 crore, equivalent arithmetically to 89.47% of the EBITDA increase; valid unsold production capitalizes costs, so this is a testing priority, not proof of inflated profit. EPR rose only ₹0.1554 crore and cannot alone explain the gain. Other income was ₹0.172 crore. FY23 PAT included a deferred-tax credit; FY24 comparative EPS later changed from ₹0.50 to ₹0.93 through an inconsistent weighted-share denominator. Current FY26 earnings are tested with actual present shares, not the older weighted EPS. [S01][S03–S05]

Reported FY26 CFO is ₹5.3393 crore. Three-year cumulative CFO/PAT is 0.907×, but five-year conversion is 0.621× and five-year CFO less cash capex totals minus ₹17.2949 crore. Receivables declined, yet balances aged one to two years rose from ₹0.1063 crore to ₹0.7115 crore, 19.42% of FY26 receivables. Supplier advances rose ₹1.9902 crore. A simplistic deduction of ₹2.4164 crore investing loans/advances from CFO would ignore the opposite ₹2.38 crore capital-creditor settlement in operating liabilities; applying both gives ₹5.3029 crore, close to reported CFO. [S01][S04–S06]

The September report’s bank table shows Q2 and Q3 book-versus-bank differences of ₹0.6635 crore and minus ₹0.7604 crore, with a much smaller ₹0.0317 crore Q4 difference and management explanations. The adopted October report instead prints zeros with a mismatched period label and no reconciliation. Both versions also contain conflicting quarterly-submission wording. Alongside recurring audit-trail limitations and the FY25 product-note scope discrepancy, this warrants G2 Hold despite clean main/IFC opinions. Exchange presentation queries and replies are not fraud findings or proof of restatement. The audit annexure records each issue, response, counterevidence and unresolved status. Accounting policy m additionally says post-retirement gratuity and leave encashment are not provided; the amount is ND. Known ₹0.3757 crore statutory dues and ₹0.1298 crore expenses payable are settled once in the model, with a separate ₹0.25 crore employee-benefit cash stress rather than an invented zero liability. [S01–S04][S12][S13]

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
sections.text:
The current issued-share denominator is 9,735,063 after July equity allotment and warrant conversion. At ₹102.30 it implies ₹99.5897 crore equity value and 24.38× FY26 profit; using FY26 historical EPS ₹4.73 without adjusting for current shares would understate the multiple. March equity gives a stale pre-raise P/B of 4.12×, not current P/B. Current enterprise value is ND because July receipts and subsequent deployment are not reconciled; an explicitly stale March-balance EV/EBITDA diagnostic is about 13.13× and is not labeled current. Remaining warrants could expand shares 35.03%, corresponding to 25.94% dilution of an unchanged existing holding, not the same percentage. [S01][S09][S10][S15][S17]

The six-row bear/base/bull model uses external manufacturing, trading, EPDM, pyrolysis and EPR revenues; explicit margins, tax, working capital, capex, debt service, issue costs, reserve cash and optional conversion cash; and exact 20 October 2031 cash boundaries. The base terminal run-rate revenue is ₹107.52 crore and EBITDA ₹20.56 crore under assumptions, valued at 8× EBITDA. Its algebraic per-share equity diagnostic is ₹178.32, not a target, because funding is unverified and its cash path breaches the reserve floor. Bear and bull diagnostics do not become investable returns either. All ordinary returns, entry prices and DCF intrinsic values are null; any non-rescue conditional return is also null after a pre-entry or later cash-floor breach. [S01][S07][S09–S11][S14]

A 3×3 growth/exit-multiple grid, 12/15/18% hurdle fields, eight linked stresses, separate counterfactual rescue cases and an FCFF DCF with 13–17% WACC, 2–4% terminal growth and explicit terminal reinvestment are embedded. DCF cash flows deduct changes in required operating cash; terminal ROIC includes that cash so terminal reserve growth is not double-counted. Signed reserve deficits are retained. The reverse-growth scan finds no feasible funded crossing, so P remains NS and no endpoint is reported as required CAGR. Operational property receives no second asset value. These computations show what must be funded and executed; they do not certify cash availability.

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent Loss Path
sections.text:
The central permanent-loss path is a sequence, not one weak ratio: scrap/energy costs or product pricing compress reclaim spreads; trading produces turnover but little cash margin; EPR pricing weakens; commissioning takes longer and ties up advances; receivable and inventory days rise; and overdraft/debt service competes with unfinished capex. A business can report accounting growth while needing expensive recapitalization before that growth produces distributable cash. The bear model therefore combines lower margins and EPR pricing, delayed production ramps, longer working-capital cycles, ongoing capex and partial working-line recall. Its negative notional cash is a funding deficit, not silently renamed debt or assumed lender support. [S01][S07][S11]

Counterfactual rescue finance is modeled separately at ₹60/share with 3% fees, shares rounded up to the next whole share, and enough upfront net cash to keep every modeled cash floor positive. This is not an available transaction or a prediction that shareholders will approve it. The bear rescue requires about ₹29.21 crore net and materially dilutes owners; a positive terminal algebraic value after such an assumed rescue does not imply an acceptable current investment. The March-to-July linear-spending checks also show pre-raise model gaps, which are explicitly hypothetical timing tests, not evidence of an actual default. The positive countercase is that July cash was actually raised, FY26 operating cash improved and the auditor reported no default. D 4 balances real buffers with material stress impairment; it is not a second hidden discount applied to every score.

sections.title: Five Times and Ten Times Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold price outcomes over five years require annual price growth of 37.97% and 58.49%, respectively, before dividends. They cannot be inferred from “4,200 tonnes/month” or a small starting market cap. At ₹511.50 and ₹1,023 per share, full exercise of currently outstanding warrants would require terminal equity values of about ₹672.38 crore and ₹1,344.75 crore. At a 20× exit P/E and 10% attributable net margin, required revenue is about ₹336.19 crore and ₹672.38 crore, or approximately 53.2% and 76.0% annual growth from FY26 revenue. A 15× terminal P/E raises those revenue requirements further. These are hurdle decompositions, not revenue targets or probabilities. [S01][S09][S10][S17]

Such outcomes also require incremental assets and working capital, manufacturing qualification, profitable output rather than only installed input capacity, and financing without still more dilution. No credible current market-share denominator or verified demand contracts support the required scale. The modeled bull case has much lower terminal revenue than the fivefold 20×/10%-margin requirement and itself assumes optional conversion plus an unverified cash-deployment path. Classification of both outcomes: Speculative / unsupported on current evidence. They could be revisited after several periods of commissioned-volume disclosure, stable product economics, cash conversion and an internally funded expansion record, not by extending a promotional TAM.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
The first decision-changing item is a reconciled FY26 bank-stock/book-debt disclosure that explains the September figures and October adopted zero table, with consistent period labels and auditor treatment. Next are verified audit-trail operation and a bridge for FY25 standalone/consolidated sales classification and FY24 EPS comparatives. A response resolving a presentation typo should be recorded as such rather than continuing to count it as an unresolved financial error. Main and IFC audit opinions must continue to be distinguished from these specific annexures. [S01–S04][S12][S13]

For funding, require published post-July sources and uses, unrestricted cash/debt availability, remaining legally committed capex, term repayments, tax/capital-creditor settlement and the UAE funding/deployment amount. Do not insist on inaccessible private daily bank statements if public evidence and conservative stress suffice. For economics, track manufactured tonnage and realization by grade; scrap yield and energy cost; EPR tonnes, prices, cash receipts and vintage; aged receivables; supplier advances including related-party delivery; EPDM/pyrolysis permits, commissioned throughput, customer acceptance and first positive cash contribution. A claim of commercial production without saleable output is insufficient. [S01][S07][S09–S11][S14]

For implementation, rebuild complete 20/60-session histories, distinguish absent records from verified no-print days, verify lot/circuit/surveillance changes and test whole-lot exit at the actual proposed position. A sustained reduction in advances and aged balances together with cash-funded expansion is thesis-positive; repeated unexplained note changes, increasing connected balances, unpaid obligations or capex funded only by optional warrants is thesis-negative. This is a research checklist, not a claim that a recurring monitoring service has been scheduled.

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved is the appropriate research classification. It is not Avoid — governance, because the available adverse evidence does not establish severe diversion or manipulation and GOV is 4 rather than ≤3. It is not Attractive or Accumulate, because G2 and G3 are unresolved and there is no investable return model. It is not a compounder: MOAT, CAP, GOV and CASH do not meet the required strength, and quality/valuation coverage is incomplete. The descriptive 6.1 GQS reflects real underlying value growth, not permission to rank the security alongside fully reliable records. [S01–S07]

For a hypothetical new position, the ₹5 lakh reference amount is not a suitability recommendation. One official lot is 1,500 shares or ₹153,450 at the reference close. Three lots cost ₹460,350; four cost ₹613,800. The conservative observed 60-session turnover basis implies 20.89 theoretical days at 5% participation, but nine observations are missing and only one observed session supports even one whole lot at that participation. Therefore no implementation conclusion is disguised as a smooth daily liquidation estimate. An existing holder faces a different problem from a new buyer, with position size, tax and liquidity preferences not supplied here. [S17–S19]

The research can be upgraded only after the financial/version and funding bridges are resolved, not merely if the price falls. At that point update balance-sheet availability, cash-floor feasibility, actual dilution and the required margin of safety, then rerun R, P, L and IAS without carrying forward today's missing factors as neutral points.

sections.title: Sources Assumptions and Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary records comprise FY20–22 prospectus restatements; FY23–26 annual reports and complete statutory audit annexures; the later adopted FY26 report; earnings call and presentation; July allotments and EGM objects; exchange clarification replies; September shareholding; UAE incorporation and director-resignation filings; official security, bhavcopy, surveillance and holiday records; dated CRISIL history; and competitor filings. Source URLs, document dates, page/section locators, original-byte hashes and safe analytical extracts are retained. Raw issuer PDFs, OCR, screenshots and shareholder identity lists are not included in analytical backups. Reproduction verifies calculations and report consistency; it does not freshly authenticate primary originals. [S01–S28]

Verified disclosure (V), calculation (C), management statement (M) and analyst assumption (A) are separated in the evidence ledger. Forecast production volumes, yields, realizations, margins, working-capital days, capex, issue costs, debt repayment and UAE external setup burn are assumptions, not undisclosed company guidance. No assumed release of supplier advances, bank deposits, operating reserve cash or optional warrant money fills a proven funding source. A subsidiary subscription is not automatically a group outflow. Cash deficits remain signed and dividends are not invented.

Open questions with direct score consequences are the adopted-report reconciliation; product-note perimeter bridge; verified current sources/uses and committed capex; actual unit economics and customer concentration; EPR realization economics; and a complete executable liquidity history. Current ownership and financing counts are verified despite the stale security-master capital field. Unknowns use ND/NS; no missing factor is assigned zero, five or a peer average. Nominal pretax INR analysis uses a 15% five-year equity hurdle with 12% and 18% sensitivity.

formula_dictionary.reported_EBITDA: Operating EBIT + depreciation; excludes other income.
formula_dictionary.normalized_EBIT: Reported operating EBIT + separately identified prior-period expense; EPR remains operating.
formula_dictionary.NOPAT: Normalized operating EBIT × 75%; analytical tax assumption, no automatic loss tax shield.
formula_dictionary.CFO_PAT: Sum of reported operating cash divided by sum of PAT across the same years; interest is financing under the reported Indian GAAP cash flow.
formula_dictionary.FCF_proxy: Reported CFO less reported cash capex; not necessarily distributable owner earnings.
formula_dictionary.incremental_ROIC: Change in normalized NOPAT / change in broad committed operating capital over fixed 3- and 5-year organic windows.
formula_dictionary.current_ROIC: NOPAT / average broad IC, descriptive only; not substituted for incremental CAP.
formula_dictionary.EV_equity: EV + signed cash less operating reserve - debt, divided by issued/diluted shares; no separate value for operating property.
formula_dictionary.DCF: Present value of post-entry FCFF less reserve increments and remaining legacy obligations; entry cash minus reserve stays signed; terminal g/ROIC reinvestment includes operating cash.
formula_dictionary.liquidity_days: Reference position / (participation × lower observed mean/median turnover); missing dates not imputed and whole-lot constraint checked separately.
